# Protocol: Twitter clusters from the authors' sample10 mirror, batch 2 (frozen 2026-10-20, before any download)

**Purpose.** Continue [the sample100 extension](twitter_sampled_extension_protocol.md) with the remaining clusters from 25 to 54 that neither this repository nor SIEVEREPRODUCTION has run and that fit the memory gate, after two traces whose results are complete were deleted to make room ([data_removed_20261020.md](data_removed_20261020.md)).

**Inputs (fixed now).** From the CMU PDL mirror used by the artifact (`.../twemcacheWorkload/cacheDatasets`): `twitter/sample10/cluster{N}.oracleGeneral.sample10.zst` for **N in {25, 28, 30, 33, 34, 36, 42, 44, 47, 51}** (10% spatial samples) and `twitter/sample100/cluster27.oracleGeneral.sample100.zst` (a 1% sample; cluster 27's sample10 file would be larger). Selection rule, applied before downloading: every cluster in 25-54 that is not already covered (our full-size runs: 26, 31, 35, 38, 39, 45, 48, 49, 50, 53; batch 1: 32, 37, 40, 43, 46, 52, 54) **and** whose file holds at most 12.5 M distinct objects, the size at which the amended peak-memory estimate (1 GiB + 250 bytes per object) stays within the available-memory gate. Object counts come from SIEVEREPRODUCTION's public `twitter_choice.tsv` (`est_obj`); the exact count is recomputed from the file. **Excluded by the rule:** clusters 29 and 41 (about 25 M objects each). Cluster 27 uses sample100 because that is the file SIEVEREPRODUCTION chose for it. Total download about 27 GB; files whose HEAD length differs from what arrives are rejected.

**Everything else is as in batch 1:** 12 policies (FIFO, LRU, CLOCK, SIEVE, ARC, TwoQ, LIRS, LHD, CACHEUS, Hyperbolic, TinyLFU snapshot, B-LRU), capacities 0.1% and 10% of the exact unique objects, sizes ignored, cold start, one thread, controlled seed 42, identity checks (SHA-256, `zstd -t`, schema, exact unique count), four workers with one result root each, runs that cannot meet a gate recorded as omitted. The worker partition balances request counts (config file).

**Reporting rule.** Results enter the Figure 3c/3f union as labelled `sample10` or `sample100` entries, never as full-trace clusters. Exact miss counts give the reductions. No hypothesis is attached; the second held-out check of ghost-informed insertion on these files is declared separately in `variant_protocol.md`, Amendment 7, also before any ghost run.

**Not done here.** Clusters 29, 41 and 32 (memory gate); full-size files; clusters 1-24 (covered by SIEVEREPRODUCTION's scaled runs).

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-20, after about 20 runs of the first attempt, before any result was used)

The first attempt let the simulator derive each capacity from its own working-set estimate. For files of 1 GiB or more (all of batch 2 except cluster 27) that estimate is sampled and ran 0.14-0.2% above the exact count (cluster 33: 1,910,084 against 1,907,377 objects), so five core-policy runs used capacities of 1,910 instead of the protocol's floor(exact x fraction) = 1,907, and the seven extra-policy runs were rejected by their own validator (`input count/footprint/capacity mismatch`). All of that attempt was **discarded** (its result directories were deleted; no number from it is used anywhere) and the batch restarted with the capacity passed explicitly as `floor(exact unique objects x fraction)` for every policy (`"exact_capacity_objects": true` in the config), which is what the protocol already said. The core policies (FIFO, LRU, CLOCK, SIEVE, ARC) are run through the seeded-baselines runner, which already supports an explicit exact capacity, instead of the first-slice runner (whose sampled-WSS exception is tied to named clusters); `sieve_repro/baseline_run.py` gained those five entries (the build is the same seeded-baselines binary; its SIEVE anchor was already verified equal to the production counters). Batch 1 files are under 1 GiB, their simulator estimate equals the exact count (checked on all 144 runs), and they are unchanged.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-20, night; after the first full pass, before any result was used)

With four workers and the Amendment-1 batch-1 estimate (1 GiB + 250 bytes per object), about half of the 264 runs were omitted by the available-memory gate (6 GiB free, 4 GiB headroom rule): the estimates were 5-7 GiB, while the measured peak RSS of every completed run (batch 1 and batch 2, up to 11.6 M objects) was at most 1.1 GB. For batch 2 the estimate is lowered to **1 GiB + 100 bytes per unique object** (largest: cluster 36, 7.1 M objects, 1.7 GiB). This changes only the pre-run gate; the live guards (12 GiB process-tree RSS, 4 GiB MemAvailable) are unchanged and still abort runs that really need the memory. Completed runs are kept; every omitted run is retried unchanged. The estimate is not part of any run identity.

## Outcome (2026-10-21)

**263 of the 264 planned exact-counter runs completed** (11 files x 2 cache sizes x 12 policies; cluster 27 only has the 0.1% and 10% runs of its sample100 file). Retry passes after the memory-gate omissions are listed under `local_results/twitter_sample10_extension/worker*/omission_logs/`. The one run that never completed is **CACHEUS on cluster 25 at the 0.1% cache**: on all four attempts made with 12-14 GB of memory available it crossed the 12 GiB live process-RSS guard and was stopped, so it is a genuine resource blow-up, recorded as omitted (`omitted.csv`). Cluster 25 therefore has 11 of 12 algorithms at 0.1% and is left out of that panel's union. Results: `sample10_extension.csv`; identity records `cluster*_identity.json`. Cluster 27 is the 1% file, the other ten are 10% samples.
